From: Reservations, Coral Bay Hotel
To: Laura Bennett
Subject: Your booking confirmation

Dear Ms. Bennett,

Thank you for choosing Coral Bay Hotel. We are pleased to confirm your reservation for a Deluxe Garden Room from March 4 to March 7. Your rate of $95 per night includes breakfast for two people, served in the Lagoon Restaurant from 6:30 to 10:30 A.M.

Check-in time is 2:00 P.M., and check-out is at 12:00 noon. If you arrive early, you are welcome to leave your bags at the front desk and use the swimming pool while your room is being prepared.

We also offer a shuttle from the airport for $15 per person. To request this service, please reply to this e-mail at least 24 hours before your arrival and include your flight number.

We look forward to welcoming you.

Kind regards,
Nina Porter
Reservations Manager

Brightway Language Centre
Home | Courses | Teachers | Contact

English for Hotel Staff

Our eight-week English for Hotel Staff course is designed for people who work, or want to work, in hotels and resorts. Lessons focus on the situations you meet every day: greeting guests, handling bookings on the phone, explaining hotel services, and dealing politely with complaints.

Classes meet on Tuesday and Thursday evenings from 6:30 to 8:30 P.M., so you can study after work. Each group has no more than 12 students, and every student receives a free online workbook.

The course fee is $240. Students who register before August 20 receive a 10% discount. A certificate is given to everyone who attends at least 14 of the 16 lessons.

Not sure which level is right for you? Take our free 20-minute placement test online, or visit our office Monday to Friday between 10:00 A.M. and 5:00 P.M.

Thank you for your understanding.

texts.body:
Software Firm Moves to Larger Offices
By Hannah Cole, Business Reporter

SEAVIEW CITY - Brightline Software, a company that makes booking programs for small hotels and guesthouses, will move its headquarters to the new Harbor Point building next month. The company's current office on Market Street has become too small for its growing team.

Brightline was founded six years ago by Carlos Mendes and Jenny Park with only four employees. Today it has 85 staff members, and it plans to hire 30 more by the end of next year, mostly programmers and customer support staff.

"Our customers are mainly family-run hotels, and they need quick, friendly support," said Ms. Park. "The new office gives us room for a 24-hour help center."

The Harbor Point building also has a large training room, which Brightline will use for free monthly workshops for hotel owners. The first workshop, on online marketing, is scheduled for May 14. The Market Street office will be taken over by a local accounting firm.

42 Orchard Lane, Westbury

September 3

Mr. Victor Almeida
18 Pine Street, Westbury

Dear Mr. Almeida,

Our records show that it has been almost a year since your last general health check. We recommend a yearly check for all adult patients, and we would like to invite you to make an appointment at your convenience.

Starting October 1, Greenfield Family Clinic will introduce a new online booking system. Patients will be able to choose a doctor, see available times, and receive reminders by text message. Appointments can still be made by phone, but the online system is usually faster.

Please also note that our clinic will now accept Harbor Health insurance cards in addition to the plans we already accept. Remember to bring your card and a list of any medicines you currently take to your visit.

If you have questions, please contact our front desk at 555-0147.

Sincerely,
Dr. Irene Walsh
Clinic Director

texts.body:
Shared Offices Gain Popularity Among Small Firms
By Marcus Hill

Five years ago, the idea of several small companies sharing one office floor was unusual in Seacliff. Today, at least a dozen shared workspaces operate in the city center, and most of them report waiting lists.

According to a recent survey by the Seacliff Business Association, the main attraction is cost. A shared desk can cost less than half of what a company would pay to rent and furnish a traditional office. Tenants also avoid long contracts, since many workspaces allow members to sign up month by month.

However, not everyone is convinced. Architect Laura Diaz, who designed two of the city's newest workspaces, warns that open layouts can be noisy. "Companies that handle confidential information, such as law firms, often find that they still need private rooms," she said. Several operators have responded by adding soundproof phone booths and small meeting rooms that can be reserved by the hour.

Operators expect demand to keep rising. Harbor Hub, the largest provider, will open a third location near the train station in March. Its manager, Tom Becker, noted that nearly 40 percent of its current members are start-ups with fewer than five employees.

You can now request refills of your regular medicine without waiting in line. Simply log in to your patient account, select the medicine you need, and choose a pickup time. Most orders are ready within four hours. If you request a refill after 6:00 P.M., it will be ready the next morning.

From: Sofia Martins, Front Office Manager
To: Front Desk Team
Subject: Wilson Tours group - Friday

Hi everyone,

As you know, a group of 48 guests from Wilson Tours will arrive this Friday. Their bus is expected at around 3:30 P.M., which is also when most of our other guests check in, so the lobby will be very busy.

To avoid long lines, the tour leader, Mr. Adeyemi, has already sent us the guests' passport details, and all room keys will be prepared in advance. Please place each key card in an envelope with the guest's name and a welcome drink voucher. Mr. Adeyemi will hand out the envelopes himself on the bus, so the group will not need to stop at the front desk at all.

Because several guests in the group do not eat meat, I have asked the kitchen to add more vegetarian dishes to Saturday's breakfast buffet.

Finally, I need one volunteer to work a later shift on Friday, until 11:00 P.M. Please let me know by Wednesday.

Thanks,
Sofia

texts.label: Job posting
texts.body:
Palm Crest Resort - Now Hiring

Palm Crest Resort, a family resort on Karon Beach, is looking for friendly and reliable people to join our team for the high season.

Front Desk Agent (full-time): Good spoken English required. Previous hotel experience preferred.

Guest Relations Officer (full-time): Fluent English. A second foreign language, such as Chinese or Russian, is an advantage.

Restaurant Server (part-time, evenings): No experience needed. Training provided.

All staff receive free meals during their shifts, a uniform, and transportation from the town center.

To apply, e-mail your resume to Chloe Barnes in Human Resources by November 30. Interviews will take place during the first week of December. Applicants for full-time positions will also be asked to complete a short English test on the day of their interview.

texts.label: E-mail
texts.body:
From: Lina Morales
To: Chloe Barnes
Date: November 18
Subject: Guest Relations Officer position

Dear Ms. Barnes,

I am writing to apply for the position of Guest Relations Officer at Palm Crest Resort, as advertised on your website. For the past two years, I have worked at the tour desk of a shopping mall in Patong, where I help visitors plan their trips, answer phone calls, and manage bookings for boat tours. Before that, I studied hospitality at Coastline College.

I speak English and Spanish fluently, and I am currently taking a Russian course on weekday evenings. I would be glad to work any shift, including weekends.

I have attached my resume. I am available for an interview at any time, except on December 3, when I will be taking my final Russian exam.

Thank you for your time.

Sincerely,
Lina Morales

Andaman Blue Ferries - Timetable (November 1 to April 30)

Harbor Town Pier to Coral Island
Departs 8:00 A.M. - Arrives 9:30 A.M. - Standard ferry
Departs 10:30 A.M. - Arrives 11:15 A.M. - Speedboat
Departs 1:00 P.M. - Arrives 2:30 P.M. - Standard ferry
Departs 4:30 P.M. - Arrives 5:15 P.M. - Speedboat

Coral Island to Harbor Town Pier
Departs 9:00 A.M. - Arrives 10:30 A.M. - Standard ferry
Departs 3:00 P.M. - Arrives 3:45 P.M. - Speedboat
Departs 5:30 P.M. - Arrives 7:00 P.M. - Standard ferry

Fares (one way, per person): Standard ferry $12, Speedboat $25. Children under 6 travel free.
Each passenger may bring one large bag free of charge. Bicycles cost an extra $5.
Tickets can be bought at the pier or online. Please arrive at least 20 minutes before departure.

From: Andaman Blue Ferries Customer Service
To: Henry Osei
Date: January 12
Subject: Change to your booking

Dear Mr. Osei,

Thank you for booking with Andaman Blue Ferries. Unfortunately, the boat you reserved for January 14 from Harbor Town Pier at 10:30 A.M. will not operate that day because of engine repairs. We apologize for the inconvenience.

We have moved your booking for two adults to the 1:00 P.M. departure on the same day. As this trip uses our standard ferry, the difference in price has been returned to your credit card. Your return trip from Coral Island on January 16 has not changed.

If the new time is not convenient, you can choose another departure or request a full refund by replying to this e-mail before January 13.

Kind regards,
Paula Nguyen
Customer Service
